knowledgeAnswers.rationale: Warning signs such as sparking, damaged insulation or overheating require immediate cessation, and the equipment is isolated and reported. Housings are not opened by workers.
The return-to-service control requires an authorised competent person to assess or repair, and a supervisor to confirm and record clearance before the machine returns to service.
Only trained and authorised operators use equipment, and unauthorised repair is not allowed. An out-of-scope request is referred.
The recognise warning signs section says a burning smell, along with other listed signs, requires immediate cessation.

practicalCriteria: Learner inspects a supplied machine and its supply with the set checklist and notes each fault found.
Learner isolates a supplied machine by switching it off, disconnecting the supply, releasing stored pressure and waiting for moving parts to stop, before any inspection.
Learner responds to a supervisor-set fault by making the equipment safe, labelling a faulty portable item, referring a fixed-installation fault, and recording the time, symptoms and person notified.
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
evidenceRequired: Simulation record with steps, times, faults found and response
Supervisor observation record against the criteria
stopWorkCriteria: Learner opens or works on a machine while the supply is still connected
Learner attempts to repair a fixed electrical installation
Learner relies on the switch alone to isolate equipment
